summary: The rank-eight multiplicity-three continuation addresses all 3,527 supplied exact-multiplicity-three rings: 3,506 general exclusions, 16 models and 5 unresolved cases. Every recorded model admits a unitary realization. The remaining rings retain unresolved status for general complex categorification. The rank-seven multiplicity-five continuation addresses all 5,805 supplied exact-multiplicity-five rings: 5,804 general exclusions, 1 realization and 0 unresolved cases. The classification of the supplied census is complete through multiplicity 5. The new realization R7_5_5678 is Rep(AGL(1,7)). The two earlier rank-six questions remain open. The historical 38-case inventory keeps its original scope.
coverage_notes: Ranks two, three and four are classified without a multiplicity restriction. Exactly fifteen rank-four Grothendieck rings occur, and every rank-four categorification admits a spherical structure. The table records the separate finite censuses.

The bound is the largest multiplicity included in the displayed census, not necessarily a complete classification range. Rank six is complete through multiplicity three; its exact bands 5, 6, 7 and 9 are also complete, while bands 4 and 8 each contain one open case.

paragraphs: Every odd generalized pivotal rotation must factor through a cyclic spin character. All 1,144 tested blocks pass. The all-order path-Clifford divisibility condition for the source family holds exactly at even parameter values, including the parameter four of this case.
The unique rank-26 modular candidate and rank-22 based-module witness remain necessary data. No compatible associators, coherent module category or general obstruction is established.

paragraphs: In the positive spherical representative, saturated modular representations determine all indicator sequences and every central phase mass. The eight spin objects form four dual pairs, all with restriction 2X+2gX+sigma+3T.

open_cases.heading: Exact multiplicity three
paragraphs: The new band contains 3,506 recorded general exclusions, 16 unitary models and 5 unresolved tensors. Each remaining tensor has an individual attempt record, distinguishing completed necessary-condition tests, unsuccessful model searches, ineligible tests and time limits.

These are investigated categorification candidates, not asserted fusion categories or established exotic examples. Passing necessary conditions supplies no associator. Failing to find a model does not prove nonexistence. Exact tensors are in data/remaining_cases.py; the per-case record is evidence/rank8_creative_20261022/per_ring_research_audit.json.

These remaining rings are extensively investigated exotic candidates in the operational sense: each survived the documented case-specific campaign of known and newly developed exclusions and model searches, including complete finite domains and specified unbounded construction families. This designation does not assert existence or novelty of a future realization.

In the stated finite center systems, R8_3_928 has four exact integer-phase witnesses and six pattern exclusions certified by complete branching trees with 49 exact Farkas leaves; R8_3_941 retains 14 patterns, with 11 integer witnesses and 3 open integer-feasibility questions in its earlier Gram test. These witnesses are necessary data, not categorical models; uncertified numerical failures are not exclusions.

replay_sections.heading: Rank six: a combined verification campaign
paragraphs: The complete initial process checked all 25,362 exclusion certificates: 25,355 passed and seven failed. Each of those seven then passed the complete unchanged checker under SymPy's Python backend. Exact matrix comparison attributes the failures to equation ordering or orientation and positional separating-vector conventions; no proof inequality or certificate was relaxed.

Both post-loop checks skipped by the initial failure gate passed separately. The model registry gives 57 matches, and the multiplicity-one partition gives 39 = 18 + 21. A hash-bound aggregate validates complete certificate coverage and 299 source/input bindings.

This is a combined campaign, not a successful single full run or an all-Python full-census pass. The initial process exited with failure, and that status is preserved in the evidence. Its loaded backend/version was not measured at startup; the global python-flint installation changed from 0.8.0 to 0.9.0 during the run, so worker and child processes may have loaded different versions.
The complete-replay orchestrator has passed identity and rejection-control checks but has not itself been executed end to end. Its existence must not be reported as an additional full-census success.

theoretical_results.heading: E21 unitary realization and creative rank-eight restrictions
paragraphs: R8_3_982 is unitarily realized by the neutral triality component of the exceptional E21 chiral fusion category from SU(3)_21 into E7_1. All 512 canonical fusion coefficients are identified exactly; the construction realizes both nonregular based-module types and the algebra 1+X5. Every Morita partner of any R982 categorification has the same based fusion ring. Five rank-eight general categorification questions remain: R8_3_928, R8_3_941, R8_3_1154, R8_3_1768 and R8_3_3472. Every hypothetical categorification admits a spherical structure and has a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate; none has a braided Morita representative. New saturated-conductor and signed spectral-capacity theorems constrain all twist orders. R1768 has 39 of 40 necessary Gram/indicator branches excluded; its irrational dimension-ratio sector outside the two dimension-orbit objects has 18 or 72 simples. The final cone survives, and the 18-object option has a forced 19-dimensional Weil block with integral nonnegative distinguished products. R1154 has four forced semionic S columns and fusion matrices in all 25 histograms, which remain necessary data. R3472 has seven remaining first-action dual spectra and 400477 second-action arithmetic spectra, conditional on the specified rank-two modules. Exact integer phase counts eliminate six of the ten R928 center patterns, leaving four with exact necessary witnesses; all fourteen R941 allocations survive the stated phase refinements. Scoped construction obstructions and such witnesses neither exclude these five rings nor construct exotic categories.

theoretical_results.heading: Further rank-eight frontier investigation
paragraphs: The new arguments include simultaneous split-module representations, normal-matrix spectral support, a complete near-group TPE reduction, complete central-induction frame constraints, full character-labeled modular S and STS equations, a two-prime norm criterion for integral center objects, complete integer center decompositions and cubic Verlinde integrality, and integral Morita and relative-cohomology obstructions. Exact all-parameter filters exclude specified near-group construction routes for every original frontier tensor. General Galois-pseudo-unitarity reductions extend the scope of all seven noncommutative searches. Complete connected-algebra underlying-object filters and exact feasible center constraints describe the remaining construction possibilities; their survivors are not asserted algebras or categories.

theoretical_results.heading: Rank-eight multiplicity-three continuation
paragraphs: Unified exclusions combine negative-subring transfer, quadratic-compositum compression, weak-integral and biquadratic relative twist traces, complete signed lifting and convex central induction. Exact separation of an enlarged necessary-condition system gives a valid contradiction only after the hypotheses and complete lifting are established.

Structural arguments use module-category ranks, split-module polynomial constraints, solvability, equivariantization and Morita transport. A unitary-only positivity obstruction becomes a general exclusion only when a separate theorem proves the relevant category must admit a unitary realization.

The explicit models include near-group equivariantizations, a cyclic permutation equivariantization of three Fibonacci factors, exceptional subfactor constructions, a conformal-embedding Morita dual, ordinary groups and a twisted A6/A5 group-theoretical construction. Direct model comparisons check all 512 coefficients; the new GH(C8) Morita dual is identified by an exact coefficient bound and uniqueness in the supplied complete census. Existence does not imply uniqueness or categorical novelty.

theoretical_results.heading: Rank-seven multiplicity-five continuation
paragraphs: The new continuation combines quadratic Casimir compression, complete signed sphericalization, Galois reduction to positive dimensions, and exact simultaneous first and second center-twist moments. A separate integral case is excluded by a complete cyclic-module Morita-dual calculation and descent to dimension 148. The current manuscript gives the categorical reductions and the finite domains checked by the programs.

The center-trace certificates impose no arbitrary cutoff on root orders. The conductor-sixty extension pairs relative-trace values under modular Galois symmetry; it does not assume equality of individual paired twists. Structural reductions and unsuccessful model searches alone do not change a case to excluded.

A general equality criterion applies at any prime p congruent to one modulo four: a twist-fixed quadratic-torus vector with saturated compression eigenvalue plus or minus 1/sqrt(p) generates a representation of level p, and its nontrivial twist support lies in the corresponding Legendre class of primitive pth roots. The manuscript proves this at every prime-power level and applies p=5 to the quadratic pair.

A second uniform criterion treats the odd conductor-eight character. Its partial projections give exact mass ratios for two-primary twist orders one, two, four and eight. Duality and Galois actions fixing the complete source field then yield two finite alternatives for active twist orders. Both criteria are proved at all congruence levels and supply necessary conditions for the complete finite-certificate arguments.

R7_5_5039 is now excluded in the general complex scope by coupled fourth and eighth rotations and an integral fusion-norm inequality. An all-order relative-phase inventory covers arbitrary twist orders. Two conductor-eight branches have exact modular contradictions; the complementary branches reduce exhaustively to 48 integer trees with 96 exact separating leaves. The eighth indicators force the finite packet domain, while the final separators use fourth-rotation and fusion-integrality constraints. This is a complete source-bound argument, distinct from rejecting an individual necessary-data witness.

R7_5_3895 is also excluded in the general complex scope. Complete signed and Galois reductions, both low induction frames, every second-indicator alternative and both character labellings are covered. The final coupled-rotation systems have 240 fourth-rotation choices: 225 have exact rational contradictions, and the remaining fifteen have complete integer chains with 2,126 exact leaves. A finite integral-order calculation checks all low words without a degree cutoff and proves the necessary norm-slack parity. The complete source-bound verifier passes in normal and optimized Python with SciPy unavailable, including a repeated run in one process.

theoretical_results.heading: Rank eight: an inner-square obstruction
paragraphs: For R8_2_24, a hypothetical complex categorification has a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate with a rank-four neutral component. Saturated modular compression forces its second indicators. Conjugation by an odd invertible would fix every neutral simple label and square to conjugation by the neutral involution.

A simultaneous pivotal chart and the short weights of associator coefficients show that such a square root would yield infinitely many inequivalent tensor functors between fixed fusion categories. Tensor-functor rigidity excludes this, giving a general complex obstruction. The source and finite-weight checks support the argument within their stated scope; its categorical reasoning remains subject to independent mathematical verification.
